2. In his application under Article 102 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh the Petitioner has claimed to he owner of an area of 2.8172 acres of land appertaining to C.S. Plot No. 186 under C.S. Khatian No. 6615, C.S. Sheet No. 22 and Towzi No. 13448 of Mouza Shahar Dhaka at present Ramna, .Ward .No. 3 of Police Station Kotwali, at present Ramna in the District of Dhaka (hereinafter referred to as the case land) by way of an agreement of purchase. The petitioner allegedly entered into the said agreement for purchase of the aforesaid land on 11.4.1980 with one Syed Jamil Hasan for a consideration of Taka 30,00,000- and thereafter due. to the vendor's refusal to execute the sale deed she filed a suit for specific' performance of contract being Title Suit No. 161 of 1991 in the First Court of the learned Subordinate Judge, Dhaka which ended in compromise between the parties and the suit was decreed by a solenama judgment and decree dated 6.7.1993 and 10.7.1993. Subsequently pursuant to the said judgment the Court executed and registered Sale Deed No. 26000 on 21.9.1994 in Title Execution. Case No. 19 of 1993. Subsequently physical possession of the case land was also allegedly given to her through process of court on 27.1.1996. It has been further stated that the Government was made party in the said suit for specific performance of contract but in spite of service of summons and notice of the court, none appeared to contest the said suit. It has been further stated that neither the Rajdhani Unnayan Kartripakha (Rajuk) nor Bangladesh Railway or the City Corporation ever acquired the said land since all along it was private land and the Petitioner has purchased the same for construction of an International Standard Five Star Hotel and Shopping Centre under the name and style South East Development Corporation (Pvt.) Ltd. He has registered the project with the Board of Investment and obtained registration No. 200005122-H dated 30.5.2000 under, section II of the Board of Investment Act. 1989 for its implementation. The Project is worth Taka 584 crore and a foreign loan of U.S.$ 10 Million has also been arranged. Considering the importance of the said Project for the then ensuing NAM  conference, the Respondent No. 2 by Memo No. Sha.Pro-6/Raj-68/98/256 dated 24.5.2001 requested RAJUK, the Respondent No. 3 to issue clearance certificate and approved the plan for the said project in favour of the Petitioner. Subsequently by Memo No. Shakha 6/Raj-68/98/308 dated 26.6.2001 under the signature of Respondent No. 2, the Government represented by the Ministry of Housing and Public Works issued a letter to the Respondent No. 3 RAJUK canceling its earlier Memo dated 24.5.2001 stating that there is a news item in the daily Star on 26.6.2001 with the caption "Encroachers eyes Osmany Udyan yet again 2.81 acres of land allocated for 5 Star Hotel". 

 7. In its Affidavit-in-Opposition, the Respondent No.4 Bangladesh Railway has stated that Bangladesh Railway has exclusive possession and title over the case land since 1882 when it was acquired by the Bangladesh Railway. It has been further stated that the so called Nawab or his descendants were never owners of the land. In Title Suit No. 161 of 1991 Bangladesh Railway was not a party and that it was not bound by the alleged compromise decree. The land was acquired for Bangladesh Railway in 1882 and since then it is railway land and Rajuk has no authority to deal with such land. It has been further stated that the land of C.S. Khatian No. 16868, plot no. 186, Sheet No. 22, Ward No. 3 area 287 was acquired for Railway by declaration No. 342 and the said acquisition was notified in Calcutta Gazette on 6.9.1882 at page no. 774 Part 1. It has been further stated that the case land belonged to Bangladesh Railway. The question of having any building and shopping complex and/or a 5 Star Hotel on the same does not arise at all and the Writ Petitioner has filed the instant Writ Petition to grab, the railway land and as such the rule is liable to be discharged.
